definitions.explanation: extremely hard and concentrated practice or training, often over a sustained period

examples.japanese: {猛練習|もうれんしゅう}を{重|かさ}ねる。
{大会|たいかい}{前|まえ}に{猛練習|もうれんしゅう}に{励|はげ}んだ。
examples.english: I devoted myself to intensive practice before the tournament.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}の{猛練習|もうれんしゅう}のおかげで、{彼女|かのじょ}はついに{全国|ぜんこく}{大会|たいかい}で{優勝|ゆうしょう}した。
examples.english: Thanks to daily intensive practice, she finally won the national championship.

notes:
Describes a level of practice or training that goes far beyond normal effort — grueling, relentless, and sustained. Composed of {猛|もう} (fierce, intense) + {練習|れんしゅう} (practice). Often associated with sports, music, and martial arts in Japan, where a culture of {根性|こんじょう} (guts, perseverance) values pushing through hardship.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猛練習|もうれんしゅう}を{重|かさ}ねる — to practice intensively again and again
- {猛練習|もうれんしゅう}に{励|はげ}む — to devote oneself to intensive training
- {猛練習|もうれんしゅう}の{成果|せいか} — the results of rigorous practice
- {猛練習|もうれんしゅう}の{日々|ひび} — days of intensive training

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {特訓|とっくん} — special/intensive training (often one-on-one or focused on a weak point)
- {猛特訓|もうとっくん} — extremely intensive special training (even more intense)
- {練習|れんしゅう} — practice (neutral, general term)
- {稽古|けいこ} — practice, rehearsal (traditional arts, martial arts)
